title: Grid paths — right/down minimum sum, any-direction minimum weight, counting paths
label: ag-multi
statement: A grid of non-negative costs. Moving **only right or down** from the top-left to the bottom-right, return the **minimum total cost** of the cells you visit (both ends included).
provenance: Three reports point at grid paths: a 2025 OA "maze, 2-D matrix, shortest path to the bottom-right moving only right or down"; a Taro report (Aug 2025) "minimum path weight from point x to point y in a 2-D grid"; and Unique Paths II at 75.6% on CodeJeet. The exact statements were not given — stage wording is mine.

stages.title: Right or down only
stages.say: Moving only right or down, what is the cheapest path from the top-left to the bottom-right?

stages.title: Any direction, weighted
stages.say: Now you can move in all four directions, some cells are walls, and you start and end at arbitrary points. Minimum path weight?
stages.require: Add `GridPaths.MinPathWeight(grid, fromR, fromC, toR, toC)` returning long: negative cells are walls; cost includes both ends; −1 if unreachable.
testNames: snake path: needs left and right moves

stages.title: Count the paths
stages.say: Back to right/down moves. Some cells are blocked. How many distinct paths are there?

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: A grid of non-negative costs. Moving **only right or down** from the top-left to the bottom-right, return the **minimum total cost** of the cells you visit (both ends included).

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Right/down only, or all four directions? (Stage 1: right/down; stage 2: all four.)
- Is the cost of the start cell included? (Yes.)
- Are weights uniform (BFS works) or varied (Dijkstra)?

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Right/down moves never revisit a row above, so each cell's best cost depends only on its top and left neighbours — a single row of DP. Four-direction moves create cycles, which is exactly what breaks that order and calls for Dijkstra.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- BFS on weighted cells (BFS is only correct when every step costs the same).
- Using DP for the four-direction version.
- Forgetting to skip stale priority-queue entries.
- int overflow on large grids of large costs.
